name: Secluded Courtyard
oracle_text:
As this land enters, choose a creature type.
{T}: Add {C}.
{T}: Add one mana of any color. Spend this mana only to cast a creature spell of the chosen type or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type.
blocked_sentences: Spend this mana only to cast a creature spell of the chosen type or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type.

needs.what: Let a mana ability's spend restriction name the source's *chosen* type instead of a fixed word -- i.e. accept the existing `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` leaf (the one `subtypes` filters already take) as an entry in an ability's `mana_restriction`, and resolve it per permanent at the moment the mana is offered rather than at load time, so the restriction is whatever creature type was chosen as this land entered. Cavern of Souls, Unclaimed Territory and Path of Ancestry are the same shape.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `mana_restriction` (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:143) is the closest existing thing and it is deliberately static: the loader (src/automtg/cards/loader.py:1013-1036) demands each entry be a bare alphabetic word, lowercases it, and freezes it into `Ability.mana_restriction` as a `frozenset[str]`; `_sources_of` then copies that frozen set onto every `ManaSource` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:172) and `mana_sources` intersects it with `spell_purpose(card)`. A `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` mapping fails the `name.replace("-", "").replace(" ", "").isalpha()` shape check, so the dynamic form is rejected at load, and there is nowhere later that a chosen type could be substituted in -- the restriction is a load-time constant by construction. Every fixed value is a different card: `mana_restriction: "creature"` makes a five-colour land that casts *any* creature (strictly better than printed), and hardcoding one subtype ignores the choice the card makes on entry. No op can substitute either, because the restriction is not something that happens on resolution -- it must be consulted while the payment solver decides which sources may pay, and a mana ability may contain only `add_mana` (or one `choose_mode` of them) anyway. Scope note: the card's other two lines need nothing new -- `{T}: Add {C}` is already written in the packet's starting point, "As this land enters, choose a creature type" is a `self_enters` trigger running `choose_type` (the shape Herald's Horn already uses), and "add one mana of any color" is the `choose_mode`-of-five-`add_mana` mana ability form. Only the spend restriction is blocked.

needs.what: Make a mana spend restriction able to permit paying for an *activated ability* whose source matches, not only for casting a spell: a `purpose` derived from the ability's source permanent (its current types and subtypes) threaded into the `mana_sources(..., purpose=...)` call on the ability-activation and ability-cost-payment paths, the way `spell_purpose(card)` is already threaded into the cast paths.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The restriction plumbing only ever knows about spells. `purpose` is computed in exactly one way -- `spell_purpose(card)` over a *card*'s types and subtypes (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:68-77) -- and it is only ever passed at the four cast sites (src/automtg/engine/legality.py:845, legality.py:1035, legality.py:1042, src/automtg/engine/game.py:337). Every other `mana_sources` call, including the ones that fund an activated ability's cost, passes no purpose, and `mana_sources` drops any source whose `restriction is not None` when `purpose is None` (costs.py:62-63). So restricted mana is silently unavailable for ability costs: with the first need closed and this one left open, the land would produce coloured mana that can cast a chosen-type creature but could never activate that creature's ability, which is half of what this line prints. There is no op- or cost-level workaround, because the decision is made inside the payment solver's source filter, before any effect runs.
